Question B-004-001-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Speech audio in a transceiver is processed over the voice range used for communications audio: 300 Hz to 3 000 Hz.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "3 Hz to 300 Hz": This range stops where the communications speech passband is just beginning, so it would lose much of the intelligible voice content.
- sourceIndex 2: "300 Hz to 1 000 Hz": This starts at the right lower edge but cuts off the upper part of the speech band needed for clear voice communication.
- sourceIndex 3: "40 Hz to 40 000 Hz": This describes a very wide high-fidelity audio range, including sub-voice bass and ultrasonic content, instead of the narrower communications speech range.
